<ConflictType>Complementary information</CONFLICT_LABEL> — Documents provide different fee components, age categories, and service options without contradiction.

The retrieved documents (d1, d4, d5, d6, d7, d8, d9, d10) all describe U.S. passport costs but focus on different aspects: d1 and d8 give specific base fees and acceptance fees, d4 provides total cost ranges, d5 and d10 explain the separate acceptance fee, and d6 shows different base fees. They are complementary, detailing various fee structures, age groups (adult vs. minor), and optional services (expedited, delivery) that together answer the query.

The evidence collectively provides a comprehensive answer. d1 and d8 give the core application and acceptance fees for adults and minors. d4, d5, d6, d9, and d10 add context on total costs, separate acceptance fees, and optional add-ons. Since all are non-contradictory and address different facets of the cost structure, they can be combined into a single coherent response.

The cost of a U.S. passport varies by applicant age, document type, and services selected. For a first-time adult passport book, the application fee is $130 and a separate $35 acceptance fee is typically required, making a total of $165 [d8]. For minors under 16, the passport book application fee is $100 plus a $35 acceptance fee, totaling $135 [d8]. Additional optional fees include $60 for expedited processing and $21.36 for 1-2 day delivery of the passport book [d1]. Passport cards cost less, with a $30 application fee for adults and a $15 fee for minors, plus the same $35 acceptance fee [d1][d8].
